look_here_first: Look at bark and leaf texture together: Chinese elm has distinctive exfoliating mottled tan/orange/gray bark and small glossy, mostly singly serrate leaves; it flowers and fruits in late summer-fall.

lookalikes.differences: Ulmus crassifolia: Both can have small leaves and fall reproduction. Cedar elm has rough hairy leaves, often corky twigs, and hairy samaras; Chinese elm has exfoliating mottled bark, glossy smoother leaves, and glabrous samaras. Ulmus pumila: Siberian elm also has small leaves but lacks Chinese elm's distinctive lacebark exfoliation and has different samara/flowering timing. Ulmus alata: Winged elm has regular corky wings and spring reproduction rather than mottled exfoliating bark and fall reproduction.
